newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Oil firms developing new ways to tap African oil.
newsitem.headline: Oil firms developing new ways to tap African oil.

text.p: Oil companies and engineering companies are developing innovative ways to tap into Africa's largely unexplored offshore energy reserves.

Delegates attending the Africa Oil 1996 conference this week heard that these ranged from concrete production barges for deep water oilfield development to tension leg platforms and undersea water processing units.
ABB Gas and Oil president Kjell Almskog said floating production ships had made marginal oilfields more economic because of their flexibility and low cost compared to large North Sea-type platforms.
He said exploration and production worldwide was continuously going into deeper and deeper waters.
"At one time, not so long ago, 300m to 400m was considered pretty deep, but now it is 1,000m, 1,200m 1,600m and who knows where this is going to end?"
Most new oilfields in Africa are deep water off West Africa and Almskog said more and more deep water activity was expected which would require "new solutions".
He said the reserves off West Africa were almost twice as high as those in the North Sea, yet produced only about half of North Sea output.

Elf Congo development manager Philippe Bureau said that in the Nkossa offshore field in Congo it had been decided to opt for pre-stressed concrete hull for the production barge instead of steel to reduce maintenance costs.
"It will be able to go 30 years without any dry-docking, which is quite impossible with a steel barge," he said.
Using a barge instead of a platform would cut the cost of production as it would save about one billion French francs and ensure higher loading capacity and increased efficiency.
